A marathon is **26.2 miles**, or **42.195 kilometers**.

The distance was standardized in 1921, based on the length used at the 1908 London Olympics. The story goes that the route was set to run from Windsor Castle to the Olympic stadium in London, with the finish line positioned in front of the royal family's viewing box—resulting in the somewhat odd distance of 26.2 miles.

The event itself is named after the ancient Greek legend of Pheidippides, a messenger who supposedly ran from the town of Marathon to Athens to announce a military victory.
